title: [CS-01] Capture and review the viewed product
label: alpha
body:
As a shopper, I want to review the viewed product so I save the intended item.

Implemented: user-initiated metadata extraction, editable review, variant/condition checks, manual fallback, scoped activeTab access. Automated fixture, core, and storage tests are recorded in docs/VERIFICATION.md. Live Chrome installation and current real retailer markup need a separate smoke test; closing this implementation story does not claim those checks passed.

title: [CS-02] Universal saved cart and budget
label: alpha
body:
As a student, I want finds from different stores in one cart so I can plan within a budget.

Implemented local persistence, quantity, notes, save-for-later, budget, subtotal, retailer links. Shipping and tax are separated into comparison. See tests and docs/VERIFICATION.md.

title: [CS-03] Transparent matched-offer comparison
label: alpha
body:
As a shopper, I want to compare item, shipping, tax, membership, discounts and cashback across checked offers.

Implemented strict identity/variant/condition matching, transparent cost breakdown, missing-cost states, ranking by total/delivery/pickup/returns. Current Alpha offers are captured or entered by users, plus labeled examples. Automated live cross-retailer discovery is next-sprint scope.

title: [CS-04] Observed price history and watched alerts
label: alpha
body:
As a bargain shopper, I want a price record and observed drop/restock alerts.

Implemented timestamped price history, price/stock transition watches on capture or offer edits, in-app alerts, optional desktop notification permission. No unattended background polling in Alpha.

title: [CS-05] Local pickup, payment schedule and orders
label: alpha
body:
As a shopper, I want to compare checked pickup options and understand financing obligations.

Implemented entered pickup details and ranking, full dollar-obligation/payment schedule calculator, manual order create/update/remove and safe tracking links. No live location, financing provider or carrier feed is claimed.

title: [CS-06] Data controls, demo, docs and feedback
label: alpha
body:
As a tester, I want a working sample preview, installation instructions and ratings/written-feedback routes.

Implemented isolated samples, local backup import/export/delete, static browser preview, deterministic Alpha ZIP, release notes, quantitative/qualitative GitHub form and draft email. Participant slots remain pending rather than invented.

title: [CS-11] Validate capture on reference users’ stores
label: next-sprint
body:
As a shopper, I want reliable capture on the stores I use.

Acceptance: collect permitted real page examples; choose supported stores from tester evidence; add fixtures for their current markup; measure manual corrections; preserve editable review and unknown-state behavior. Owner: Kartik (engineering), Jake (acceptance).

title: [CS-12] Authorized automatic cross-store offer discovery
label: next-sprint
body:
As a shopper, I want matched retailer offers found automatically.

Acceptance: select an authorized feed/source; document access and refresh limits; normalize model/variant/condition; reject mismatches; label freshness and unknown shipping/tax. No AWS requirement; use the simplest permitted source integration. Owner: Kartik, with Jake prioritizing scope.

title: [CS-13] Resolve observed Alpha usability blockers
label: next-sprint
body:
As a reference tester, I want blockers fixed so save and compare are easy.

Acceptance: collect task completion/time and 1–5 ratings plus qualitative feedback; reproduce selected blockers; add meaningful regression protection; verify changes with affected testers where possible. Owner: Jake (feedback), Kartik (fixes).

title: [CS-14] Opt-in unattended price checks
label: backlog
body:
As a shopper, I want watched offers checked while I am away.

Acceptance: supported authorized source, explicit opt-in, refresh/frequency controls, source timestamps, notification deduplication, justified permissions. Requires an offer source; current Alpha evaluates user-triggered observations only.

title: [CS-15] Authorized order updates
label: backlog
body:
As a shopper, I want supported order statuses imported automatically.

Acceptance: a permitted source, safe handling of order credentials, normalized status mapping, last-sync time, manual fallback. Current Alpha order records are entered by users.

title: [REL-01] Smoke-test ZIP installation in real Chrome
label: release
body: Unzip the published Alpha asset and use chrome://extensions > Developer mode > Load unpacked. Verify toolbar opens side panel, capture works on a permitted product detail page, save/compare/watch/order/backup flows work, and no extension errors appear. Record actual browser/version and page details. Automated Chromium startup was blocked in the development Mac environment; do not infer an installation pass from DOM or fixture tests.

title: [REL-02] Recruit ten reference testers and send invitations
label: release
body:
Owner: Eashan (recruiting), Jake (test protocol), Kartik (release support).

Confirm ten consenting participants privately, assign R01–R10, personalize docs/ALPHA_EMAIL.md, send individually, and record true send dates privately. Draft email is not evidence of sending; no invented identities. Keep contact information out of public GitHub.

title: [REL-03] Collect quantitative and qualitative Alpha feedback
label: release
body: Use the Alpha feedback issue form or private email reply. Record task completion/time and ease/clarity/usefulness/confidence ratings plus confusing/missing features and highest-value improvements. Distinguish installed-extension and browser-demo results. Report actual denominators; targets are not measured outcomes.
